title: Product Designer
intro: Design the flows, screens and component systems for websites and software. We’re interested in work that shows how you resolve a task, not just how you style a screen.
responsibilities: Map user journeys, information architecture and key product workflows with the project team.
Create wireframes and interactive Figma prototypes that explain behaviour, not just appearance.
Develop responsive interface systems with reusable components, variants and design tokens.
Work with engineers on accessibility, edge cases and the quality of the finished experience.
skills: A portfolio explaining your role, design decisions and the problem each project addresses.
Strong Figma skills, including components, auto layout, prototyping and developer handover.
An understanding of responsive layouts, keyboard interaction and accessible interface patterns.
Clear communication and the ability to explain trade-offs using evidence and project constraints.
portfolio: Share two or three relevant projects. Include the original challenge, your contribution, examples of iteration and what you learned. Show flows or interaction states alongside final screens.

title: Creative Developer (WebGL)
intro: Build websites with React, TypeScript and real-time graphics. The work combines frontend development with WebGL, scroll animation and practical performance testing.
responsibilities: Build responsive interfaces and reusable components with React, TypeScript and modern CSS.
Develop Three.js or WebGL scenes and connect animation to scrolling and pointer interaction.
Profile loading, rendering and memory use across desktop and mobile devices.
Provide keyboard-friendly interactions, reduced-motion behaviour and useful graphics fallbacks.
skills: Working examples of interactive websites or graphics with a clear explanation of your contribution.
Confidence with JavaScript or TypeScript, browser APIs and component-based development.
Practical knowledge of Three.js, shaders or equivalent real-time graphics tools.
Attention to frame timing, asset optimisation, cleanup, accessibility and maintainable code.
portfolio: Send live demos and, where shareable, code samples or repository links. Explain performance constraints, fallback behaviour and the decisions you made for different devices.

title: Brand Designer
intro: Develop visual identities from initial direction through to finished assets. Show us how your typography, colour and composition hold together across different applications.
responsibilities: Translate business context and audience needs into coherent creative directions.
Develop marks, wordmarks, typography, colour systems and composition rules.
Test identities across realistic digital and print touchpoints, including small-scale use.
Prepare editable assets, production exports and guidelines that other people can apply.
skills: A portfolio showing identity systems and their applications, rather than isolated logos alone.
Strong typography, composition, colour and vector artwork skills.
Confidence preparing SVG, PDF and raster exports for their intended uses.
The ability to present a visual direction clearly and respond constructively to feedback.
portfolio: Choose identity projects that show the reasoning behind the direction. Include concept development, practical applications, your individual contribution and examples of usage guidance.

title: Motion Designer
intro: Create brand animation, product sequences and web-ready motion assets. We’re interested in timing, composition and how you prepare the work for its final format.
responsibilities: Develop storyboards, style frames and motion concepts around a clear communication goal.
Create brand motion, product animation and transitions for agreed channels and formats.
Collaborate with designers and developers on motion that can be delivered effectively on the web.
Prepare organised source files, optimised exports and clear notes for implementation.
skills: A focused reel or case studies demonstrating timing, composition and storytelling.
Experience with relevant tools such as After Effects, Blender or Cinema 4D.
An understanding of codecs, transparency, resolution and export trade-offs.
Careful attention to iteration, feedback and the context in which an animation will be viewed.
portfolio: Share a short reel plus one or two project breakdowns. Identify the parts you created, the tools used and how the final assets were prepared for delivery.
